# Frozen scalar DSP oracle, version 1

These expected values were produced on 2026-10-23 by the independent C scalar
DSP, before its test driver was removed. They were **not** generated by the
Rust implementation. A fresh build and two fresh renders matched the earlier
oracle output byte for byte, and the executable hash matched too.

The Rust tests embed these files. They don't compile C, start processes, read
the old source tree, or write new expected values.

## Qualified targets

The numerical results are qualified for **Linux x86_64 and aarch64,
little-endian**. ARM was added after an isolated Cortex-A53 QEMU run, using the
Pro II stock runtime, matched the original fixtures in mono and stereo with no
differing F32 samples and zero maximum audio error. No expected audio bytes or
meter tolerances were changed for it. The probe is kept in
`.local/arm-scalar-probe-20261023`, and its output is in
`.local/rust-all-sources-arm64.zs5gaIGp/build/checks/arm-scalar-probe.log`.

The test still refuses to build for other architectures until they are
qualified. Windows behaviour tests are separate. The ARM result comes from
emulation, so it shows functional agreement only. Device timing, models and
recovery aren't covered here.

Copies of the original generator and sources, build and runtime metadata, and
the fresh raw output are kept in `.local/rust-dsp-golden.daIS4jmt`. Earlier
evidence is in `.local/rust-dsp-oracle-1792768055044714121`. These
directories are provenance archives. The ordinary tests don't need them.

To regenerate the fixtures on purpose, use a separately reviewed independent
oracle and update the provenance. Don't replace these files with Rust output
to make a failing test pass. The production C source is still kept elsewhere
until it is retired more broadly.

## Scenario and record format

Both fixtures use 48 kHz, 180 blocks and 43,280 samples per channel. Block
sizes cycle through `[112, 7, 480, 1, 240, 63, 1024, 13]`, and the last cycle
is partial. Each block stores, in order:

1. `n` little-endian IEEE F32 samples for each channel, left then right.
2. Four little-endian IEEE F64 meters: input peak, output peak, sum of squares,
   gain reduction.
3. Two little-endian U64 counters: samples and clipped samples.

Audio is compared **bit for bit** and counters exactly. Each floating-point
meter must satisfy `abs(actual-expected) <= 1e-10 * max(abs(expected), 1)`,
the original tolerance. The tests require the exact fixture length and that
every record is consumed. Embedded FNV64 fingerprints catch accidental fixture
changes in the ordinary tests without a cryptographic dependency in the DSP.
`SHA256SUMS` provides cryptographic hashes for independent checks.

### Input

The input uses unsigned 32-bit arithmetic:
`q = (((frame*1664525 + 1013904223 + channel*97) >> 8) & 65535) - 32768`,
then `q/65536` as F32. These overrides apply in order: frames that are
multiples of 997 are NaN, multiples of 991 are positive infinity, and
multiples of 983 are -20. This exercises the finite-value guard and values
above unity.

### Chain

The chain starts in the default effect order with suppression off. The
generator aborts if suppression is constructed or used. The enabled stages
are:

- High-pass at 80 Hz.
- Compressor: threshold -18 dB, ratio 3, attack 10 ms, release 120 ms, makeup
  2 dB.
- Gain -3 dB.
- Limiter: ceiling -1 dB, release 100 ms.
- EQ: input -4 dB, output 2 dB.

The left EQ has seven bands, one of each existing type. In stereo, the right
channel has six independent bands with offset values. Band `i` uses frequency
`75+401*i+73*right`, gain `(-1 if i odd else 1)*(1.5+i)`, Q `.41+.23*i`,
alternating APO and RLC modes, slope 1 and width 1. The Rust scenario code is
the same code that was compared against the oracle. Its band, config and
sample source span is pinned in the provenance.

### Changes during the run

| Block boundary | Persistent change unless a range is stated |
| --- | --- |
| 20 | High-pass 140 Hz, gain -9 dB, band 1 frequency 510 Hz / gain -7 dB, EQ input -2 dB |
| 40 | Swap left bands 1 and 5 |
| 41 | Solo left band 2 |
| 42 | Truncate left EQ to five bands during the structural transition |
| 60 | Remove independent right EQ; use shared settings |
| 80–89 | Disable EQ |
| 100–119 | Bypass the chain |
| 130–139 | Disable compressor and limiter |
| 150 | 32-band cascade, frequency `30+700*i`, alternating ±12 dB; EQ input and output both -36 dB |

These changes cover coefficient smoothing, band ID and history handling, rapid
structural crossfades, linked stereo dynamics, bypass smoothing and arbitrary
block sizes. Add new scenarios as separate fixtures and leave this one
unchanged.
